name: SMA ablation cath.
full_name: NC State SMA-actuated robotic ablation catheter (Buckner lab)
group: North Carolina State University, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Electro-Mechanics Research Laboratory (G. D. Buckner; J. H. Crews, J. H. Wiest); NIH SBIR 5R44HL095227 (no company named)
versions: 2008 Veeramani, Buckner et al.: modelling (Smart Mater. Struct.) and design and control (ASME DSCC) of an SMA-actuated robotic catheter, cited by crews2012 and wiest2015 (not read); 2012 JIMSS design optimisation of single-tendon and antagonistic SMA segments in COMSOL with a genetic algorithm, tested on planar wire rigs (crews2012_design, full); 2015 RAS path optimisation and control of a two-segment, eight-tendon catheter (wiest2015_path, full); the lab's later bedside robot is robots_A3 portable_kantu2025 (NC State/NYU), predecessor of LegoBot
devices_driven: own 2.7 mm catheter with two bending segments, each actuated by four offset SMA tendons (wiest2015 Sec. 2)
n_dof_detail: 4 bending (two segments x bend angle and orientation)
translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation (SMA tendons heated by PWM); no robotic insertion stage
device_range: 90 and 180 degrees of omnidirectional bending for the proximal and distal segments (wiest2015_path p. 93); own 2.7 mm catheter
imaging_compat: modified EnSite NavX (St. Jude) electrode localisation (wiest2015_path p. 94); trakSTAR magnetic tracking on the 2012 test rigs (crews2012_design p. 552)
validation_detail: bench: catheter submerged in a saline tank with EnSite patch electrodes; path optimisation repeated on four point sets; closed-loop control on one optimised 16-point path (wiest2015_path pp. 95-96); 2012: single-tendon rig (4 tendon offsets x 11 prestrains, 5 tests each) and four antagonistic rigs (crews2012_design p. 552-553)
key_numbers: path optimisation about 20 s; step response about 2 s with < 10 deg overshoot; mean steady-state tip error 5.5 mm, called unacceptably large by the authors; NavX uncertainty 7.1 +- 3.5 mm, imprecision +- 0.8 mm (wiest2015_path); 2012: optimal bend radius 7.0 mm (single-crystal model) and 7.6 mm (polycrystalline); experimental optimum prestrain about 3.5-4.5% and tendon offset about 1 mm (crews2012_design p. 555-556)
sim_model: yes: COMSOL finite-element models of SMA-actuated segments coupled to a genetic algorithm in MATLAB (single-crystal and polycrystalline free-energy SMA models), checked on wire rigs (crews2012_design p. 546-557); MATLAB simulations to tune the 2015 path optimiser (wiest2015_path Sec. 2.6)
sim2real_detail: none found (simulation used for design optimisation, not for a controller)
